pins.name: D3
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. Commonly wired to a FLASH/BOOT button on dev boards
Onboard "PRG" FLASH/BOOT pushbutton (active-low) — see pfodWeb NOTE above chipGpios for sources

pins.name: TX
pins.label: TX (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: RX
pins.label: RX (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D2
pins.label: D2 (GPIO4)
pins.notes: Onboard SSD1306 OLED display is wired to this pin as I2C SDA (shared general-purpose I2C bus, not exclusive - other I2C devices can still be added).

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (GPIO5)
pins.notes: Onboard SSD1306 OLED display is wired to this pin as I2C SCL (shared general-purpose I2C bus, not exclusive - other I2C devices can still be added).

pins.name: D8
pins.label: D8 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM.
